notes:
Evaluation focus: latency SLO definition and measurement alignment for Dedicated capacity. Customer is latency-sensitive (trading desk) — wants deterministic tail behavior and predictable reserved GPU sizing. Key points from meetings and technical recommendations:

- Measurement surface: customer measures end-to-end (client-side) RTT in production; Redwood measures server-side processing and queueing. Must reconcile: propose dual reporting (client-side and server-side) in SLA with clear offsets.

- Streaming vs non-streaming: define separate SLOs.
  * Non-streaming (full-response): SLOs measured as time from request received by Redwood to last-token-out on server side; client-side p95 should include network and TLS overhead. Example target: server p95 < 180ms -> client p95 < 250ms (allocating 70ms network+client).
  * Streaming (first-byte + completion): split into initial-token latency (first-byte) and time-to-last-token. Customer cares more about initial-token for interactive UX. Example targets: first-byte server p50 < 80ms, p95 < 220ms; completion p95 depends on response length (budget per token).

- Percentile definitions and collection windows: agree on p50/p95/p99 computed over 5-minute rolling windows for operational alerts and 30-day windows for SLA measurement (monthly billing). Avoid averaging percentiles — use empirical percentiles from aggregated samples.

- Client vs server timing reconciliation: include a measurement appendix in SLA. Server should publish per-request timelines: enqueue_time, start_infer_time, first_token_time, last_token_time, kv_cache_hit boolean, batch_size. Client-side can submit annotated traces for dispute resolution. Add a 1-minute sampling trace collector for postmortems.

- Warm vs cold: exclude instance cold-starts in SLA (recommend exclusion window: 10 minutes after scale-up). Also exclude scheduled maintenance and region-level outages (with defined incident windows). Define warm-up traffic policy for autoscaling tests.

- Batching and throughput effects: tail latency sensitive to batching policy. For reserved capacity sizing, we recommended:
  * Replay real traces at target QPS with Redwood test harness (S3 traces).
  * Measure p95/p99 across three modes: minimal batching, latency-optimized batching, cost-optimized batching.
  * Use the latency-optimized profile for SLA commitments; provide cost-optimized profile as optional lower-cost fallback with different SLAs.

- KV cache and prompt prefixes: cache hit ratio materially reduces p95. Capture cache-hit-tagged metrics; SLA computation should report hit vs miss percentiles separately.

- Reserved GPU planning: from customer traces (avg tokens/sec and tail percentiles), SE produced an initial sizing: 8x A100-equivalent for target 3k concurrent chats with median len 40 tokens and p95 server-first-byte <220ms. Sizing notes attached in Drive doc. Customer asked for a sensitivity table (QPS +/- 30%, token length +/- 50%).

- SLA language suggestions (draft):
  * "Redwood will maintain server-side p95 latency < 200ms for non-streaming requests measured on warm instances over a monthly window, excluding scheduled maintenance and region outages."
  * "For streaming requests, Redwood will maintain server-side first-byte p95 < 250ms and median first-byte <100ms on warm instances."
  * "Client-side p95 will be reported separately; Redwood will provide a monthly reconciliation report and sample traces for any SLA disputes."
  * "Remedies: service credit tiers tied to missed monthly p95 SLA; force majeure and maintenance carve-outs enumerated."

- Measurement tooling: customer asked for a lightweight client SDK snippet to measure exact timing points and submit anonymized telemetry to Redwood for reconciliation. Also requested access to per-request logs (token timing granularity) under NDA for one-week window during POC.

- Next actions (agreed):
  1) Redwood to run 72-hour perf replay on dedicated staging with customer's traces (owner: SE Ravi).
  2) Produce sensitivity table and updated reserved-GPU recommendation (owner: SE).
  3) Draft SLA appendix with measurement definitions and exclusion rules (owner: AE Sofia + Legal).
  4) Security to provide KMS/audit log whitepaper and residency assurances (owner: Security).

- Customer quotes / color: "We need guarantees that tail spikes won't cascade into trading decisions — p95 matters more than average." Also: "First-byte determines whether traders perceive the tool as usable during market open windows."

- Open questions / risks:
  * How to handle multi-region routing and regional fallbacks in SLA? Customer wants regional isolation for trading hours.
  * Legal insists on clearer data residency language (encryption at rest + KMS controls).
  * Billing model if customer needs burst capacity beyond reserved GPUs (definition of chargeable overage and pre-warm rules).
